title: Define the intervention proposal contract V1
businessObjective: Convert grounded intelligence into a finite, reviewable proposal without granting AI, callers, proposals, or validation dependencies authorization authority.
technicalObjective: Implement one closed Draft 2020-12 V1 proposal schema and one runtime-safe semantic validation deep module that internally uses committed authorities, validates P2-002 provenance, rejects authority claims and cross-field inconsistency, and never throws; do not implement generation, policy, approval, execution, persistence, workflow, or provider behavior.
assumptions: P2-004 remains static Tier-0 contract validation only and invokes no proposal generator or AI provider.
The proposal validator consumes untrusted proposal, intelligence request, and intelligence result data while obtaining schema and semantic authority only from committed repository modules.
A valid proposal may request a finite capability for later evaluation but cannot grant it, authorize it, or carry an executable command or target.
No production write, deployment, live credential access, retention behavior, workflow state, or external side effect is authorized.
acceptanceCriteria: The committed `schemas/intervention-proposal-contract-v1.schema.json` is a closed Draft 2020-12 authority that requires the exact diagnosis, evidence references, confidence, recommended action, alternatives, affected systems, requested capabilities, risk classification, approval requirement, verification plan, rollback plan, expected outcome, source-intelligence, and non-authority fields defined by the GOV-044 design.

The runtime-safe deep module exports only `validateInterventionProposal(proposal, intelligenceRequest, intelligenceResult)`, loads committed authority internally, uses the public P2-002 validation boundary, accepts no caller authority or dependency injection, returns deeply frozen plain-data decisions, mutates no input, and never throws.

All six outcomes, four risk classes, two approval classes, seven requested capabilities, identifier/string/number/collection bounds, deterministic reason codes, precedence, and cross-field mappings exactly match the finite design.

Validation rejects invalid or ineligible P2-002 sources, mismatched task/request/status, non-source evidence/cause/hypothesis/system references, raised or relabelled confidence, unknown capability, outcome/capability/approval/risk/rollback inconsistency, and every self-approval, authorization, execution, verification, or production-eligibility claim fail closed.

Core contract logic has no provider, transport, persistence, queue, workflow, scheduler, policy, approval, executor, verification, audit, notification, SDK, network, filesystem, credential, clock, or environment import; no AI invocation, generation, retention, or production behavior is added.

The exact admitted command `node tests/intervention-proposals/validate-intervention-proposal-contract-v1.mjs` compiles the committed authority and deterministically covers all finite values, variants, focused real exploit paths, hostile never-throw inputs, private-authority isolation, deep freeze/clone behavior, and the dependency boundary.

Packet validation, the exact P2-004 validator, `npm run verify:fast`, `git diff --check`, changed-path and secret checks, independent Sol review, task-specific machine evidence, and final-head CI pass before merge.
allowedCommands: npm run verify:task -- --task SUT-AIOS-P2-004 --verifier-agent qa-verification --verifier-model gpt-5.6-sol --acceptance-confirmed
requiredChecks: closed Draft 2020-12 schema compilation and finite-contract validation
canonical P2-002 provenance and cross-reference validation
malformed and hostile input never-throw validation
solEscalationTriggers: Any ambiguity or implementation that permits caller-supplied authority, unvalidated P2-002 provenance, provider/infrastructure imports in core, or proposal claims of approval, authorization, execution, verification, or production eligibility.

Any generation, provider call, live data access, retention, persistence, workflow, policy, approval, capability grant, executor, notification, audit-store, production write, payment, booking, inventory, pricing, RLS, migration, credential, or external behavior.
rollbackExpectations: Revert only the P2-004 schema, contract module, validator, product documentation, task-state change, risk entry, and P2-004 evidence; preserve P2-002 authorities/evidence, GOV-044/GOV-045 history, all terminal records, canonical sources, immutable snapshots, and external systems.
